what: Pre-registration of the forward test of the simple alarms as the main early-warning feature.
post_hoc: Post-hoc on one incident: these four alarms were picked as the main early warning after seeing that they fired with more harm still to come than the shared-control signs on the Swarm Traces release. Their thresholds were not tuned, but the choice of alarms (and of the 6 h volume history over the 12 h one) was made with that answer in view, so their figures on that release are not a test.

main.name: First new host after 12 h
main.what: The first action, at least 12 hours after the first action, that contacts a host no earlier action named.

main.name: First search_for_secrets action
main.what: The first action the pack labels search_for_secrets. A pack without that intent never fires it.

main.name: Distinct-actor alarm (3 sd, 12 h history)
main.what: The first hour with more distinct named actors than the mean plus 3 standard deviations of every earlier hour (at least 12 earlier hours). Known at the end of that hour.

main.name: Volume alarm (3 sd, 6 h history)
main.what: The first hour with more actions than the mean plus 3 standard deviations of every earlier hour (at least 6 earlier hours). Known at the end of that hour.

variants.name: Volume alarm (3 sd, 12 h history)
variants.what: The volume alarm with 12 hours of history: the baseline published in v2.2.0.

variants.name: First new host after 24 h
variants.what: The new-host alarm after 24 hours of history.

alarms.counted: actions with an intent and a time; an actor is named when its kind is not 'run'

alarms_sha256_how: sha256 of json.dumps(alarms, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=True) as UTF-8

context_signs.shared_place: coordination: two identities use one place
context_signs.carried_token: coordination: one identity carries another's token
context_signs.note: scored by the same measures, as context; not candidates for the main alarm

measures.fired: the alarm fires at least once in the swarm
measures.before_harm: the alarm fires strictly before the first true harmful record in the generator's truth file
measures.lead_h: hours from the alarm to the first true harm (minus = after); median over swarms where it fired
measures.harm_share: share of the true harmful records later than the alarm; 0 when the alarm never fires
measures.beats_place: harm_share of the alarm strictly greater than harm_share of the shared-place sign
measures.benign_fired: the alarm fires at least once in a benign swarm (a false alarm)

intervals.per_swarm: Wilson 95% binomial interval on k of n swarms
intervals.settings: 95% percentile interval over 1000 resamples of whole settings (scenario classes for the independent generator)
intervals.per_24h: exact (Garwood) Poisson 95% interval on alarms per 24 h of benign trace, each alarm counted once per swarm

hypotheses.name: lead
hypotheses.statement: The alarm fires before the first true harm in more than half of the coordinated swarms (lower end of the per-swarm 95% binomial interval above 0.5).
hypotheses.expected: Expected to fail: on seeds 31-40 and 501-510 every simple alarm fired at or after the first true harm.

hypotheses.name: order
hypotheses.statement: The alarm fires with strictly more true harm still to come than the shared-place sign (a sign or alarm that never fires counts as 0) in more than half of the coordinated swarms (lower end of the interval above 0.5). This is the order seen post-hoc on the real release.
hypotheses.expected: Expected to fail on the original simulator: on four swarms of seeds 21-22 (seen before, checked while this code was written) the shared-place sign had more true harm still to come every time. On the independent generator the shared-place sign fired in 0 of 20 swarms before, so there the alarms should win by default.

hypotheses.name: false alarms
hypotheses.statement: The alarm fires in fewer than 20% of the benign swarms (upper end of the per-swarm 95% binomial interval below 0.2).
hypotheses.expected: Expected to hold for the new-host alarm (0/30 and 2/50 before) and to fail for the 6 h volume alarm on the independent generator (19/50 before).

decision: Each hypothesis is decided separately for each of the four alarms and for 'any of the four', on each generator, by the per-swarm interval. No alarm, parameter or threshold is changed after the run; a failed hypothesis is reported as failed.

settings.name: quiet
settings.label: 40 agents, no hidden reads, no notes

settings.name: field_times
settings.label: 40 agents, a time field on every record

seeds_never_run: original generator: 21-30 (v2.1.0) and 31-40 (v2.2.0) have been run; 41-50 have not. Independent generator: 501-510 have been run; 511-520 have not.
limits: Written by the same people who chose the alarms, minutes before the run, in an uncommitted working tree: the order rests on this file's own time stamp and hashes unless it is committed before the results.
Both generators are ours. The simulators never write a search_for_secrets action, so that alarm cannot fire on them: its rows are not evidence of anything.
Lead before the first true harm and share of harm still to come are different measures; the real release has only the second.
rule: no swarm with these seeds exists when this file is written; run `python3 -m agenttrace.earlywarn forward23` afterwards
